name: Menahem king of Israel
charge: Ripping up the women with child at Tiphsah, and buying Assyria with money exacted from Israel
summary: Menahem came up from Tirzah, killed Shallum, and took the throne. When Tiphsah would not open to him he smote it and ripped up all the women therein that were with child. He then paid Pul a thousand talents of silver, exacted from the wealthy of Israel, to confirm the kingdom in his hand — and died in his bed.
offense: Menahem struck Tiphsah because it would not open to him and ripped up its pregnant women (2 Kings 15:16). The refusal of entry became an occasion for cruelty against those least able to resist. His rise did not bring a departure from Jeroboam's sins; he continued in them throughout his reign (2 Kings 15:17-18). When Pul of Assyria came, Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand. He exacted the money from Israel's wealthy men (2 Kings 15:19-20). The people paid for the foreign support by which their ruler sought to secure his own position.
judgment: Assyria withdrew, and Menahem died after a ten-year reign, with Pekahiah succeeding him (2 Kings 15:20-22). No separate personal penalty is recorded against him. The successful payment must not be mistaken for a judgment declaring his cruelty righteous. His son's reign lasted two years before Pekah killed him. Further Assyrian conquest and deportation followed in Pekah's days (2 Kings 15:23-29). The support purchased for Menahem did not establish lasting security for the house or nation. He had obtained time on the throne without addressing the sin that left Israel exposed to further overthrow.

verses.text: For Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, and came to Samaria, and smote Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.
And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he made, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

Then Menahem smote Tiphsah, and all that were therein, and the coasts thereof from Tirzah: because they opened not to him, therefore he smote it; and all the women therein that were with child he ripped up.
In the nine and thirtieth year of Azariah king of Judah began Menahem the son of Gadi to reign over Israel, and reigned ten years in Samaria.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not all his days from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
And Pul the king of Assyria came against the land: and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand.

And Menahem exacted the money of Israel, even of all the mighty men of wealth, of each man fifty shekels of silver, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back, and stayed not there in the land.
And the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Menahem slept with his fathers; and Pekahiah his son reigned in his stead.
In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

For so it was, that the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, which had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods,
Samaria shall become desolate; for she hath rebelled against her God: they shall fall by the sword: their infants shall be dashed in pieces, and their women with child shall be ripped up.

Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border:

text.text: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah Pekahiah the son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned two years.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.

But Pekah the son of Remaliah, a captain of his, conspired against him, and smote him in Samaria, in the palace of the king’s house, with Argob and Arieh, and with him fifty men of the Gileadites: and he killed him, and reigned in his room.

entries.commentary: Azariah, also called Uzziah, begins to reign over Judah and does that which is right in the sight of the Most High as his father Amaziah had done. The high places were not removed, so the people still sacrificed and burned incense there, an incomplete obedience. The Most High smote him so that he was a leper until his death, and he dwelt in a separate house while Jotham his son judged the people. Azariah's fuller history is written elsewhere, and the teacher directs the reader to [2 Chronicles 26](/bible/2-chronicles/26) for a more detailed account of his life and acts. -

Zachariah son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel only six months and does that which is evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Shallum conspires against Zachariah, smites him before the people, slays him, and reigns in his place. The end of Zachariah fulfills the word spoken to Jehu, that his sons would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation. -

Shallum reigns a full month in Samaria before Menahem son of Gadi goes up from Tirzah, smites him, and reigns in his stead. Menahem strikes Tiphsah and its coasts because they would not open to him, and he ripped up the women with child, a mark of his cruelty.

Menahem reigns ten years in Samaria and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Pul the king of Assyria comes against the land, and Menahem gives him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand. Menahem raises the tribute by exacting fifty shekels of silver from each mighty man of wealth, so the king of Assyria turns back and does not stay in the land.

Pekahiah son of Menahem reigns two years over Israel and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Pekah, a captain of his, conspires against him and smites him in the king's house at Samaria with fifty Gileadites, then reigns in his room. This is a military coup, where a trusted captain kills the king and seizes the throne.

Pekah son of Remaliah reigns twenty years over Israel, the same Pekah spoken of in the book of Isaiah. In his days Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes and takes Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, carrying them captive to Assyria. Hoshea son of Elah conspires against Pekah, smites and slays him, and reigns in his stead.

Jotham son of Uzziah reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem and does that which is right, according to all his father Uzziah had done. Again the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense there. Jotham builds the higher gate of the house of the Most High. In those days the Most High begins to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.

Hoshea son of Elah reigns nine years over Israel in Samaria and does evil, though not as the kings before him. Shalmaneser king of Assyria comes up, and Hoshea becomes his servant and pays tribute. The king of Assyria finds conspiracy in Hoshea because he sent messengers to So king of Egypt and stopped his yearly tribute, so he shuts him up in prison. Assyria besieges Samaria three years, then in the ninth year of Hoshea takes it and carries Israel away to Assyria, placing them in Halah, Habor, and the cities of the Medes.

This captivity comes because the children of Israel sinned against the Most High who brought them out of Egypt and feared other gods. They walked in the statutes of the heathen, built high places in all their cities, and set up images and groves on every high hill and under every green tree. They wrought wicked things to provoke the Most High and served idols, though He had said plainly, ye shall not do this thing. -

The Most High testified against Israel and Judah by all the prophets and seers, calling them to turn from evil and keep His commandments. They would not hear but hardened their necks like their fathers who did not believe in the Most High. To believe in the Most High is to take heed to the commandments, so those who claim belief while breaking the commandments do not truly believe. They rejected His statutes and covenant, followed vanity, made molten images and two calves, worshipped the host of heaven, and served Baal. They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire, used divinations and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil. -

The Most High is very angry and removes Israel out of His sight, leaving only the tribe of Judah. Judah also fails to keep the commandments and walks in the statutes that Israel made. The Most High rejects all the seed of Israel, afflicts them, and delivers them into the hand of spoilers until He casts them out of His sight. This rejection is why the seed of Israel are later called heathens and Gentiles in the New Testament, which resolves much of the struggle over Jews and Gentiles there. -

The king of Assyria brings men from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim to dwell in the cities of Samaria in Israel's place. Because they do not fear the Most High, He sends lions among them that slay some of them. One of the carried-away priests is brought back to Bethel to teach the settlers how they should fear the Most High.

Every nation makes gods of its own and sets them in the houses of the high places the Samaritans had made. The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, Cuth made Nergal, Hamath made Ashima, the Avites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burnt their children to Adrammelech and Anammelech. They feared the Most High and also served their own gods after the manner of the nations they came from. The Most High made His covenant and charged the children of Jacob whom He named Israel, showing the covenant belongs to Israel and not to all nations.

The Most High commanded Israel not to fear, bow to, serve, or sacrifice to other gods, but to fear and worship Him alone who brought them out of Egypt with a stretched out arm. They were to observe His statutes, ordinances, and commandments forevermore, and He would deliver them out of the hand of all their enemies. No nation and no treaty can redeem Israel from their condition, only turning to the Most High can. These settler nations feared the Most High yet served their graven images to this day, and as a nation Israel does the same, serving the gods of the nations. -
When Ephraim spake trembling, he exalted himself in Israel, but when he offended in Baal, he died.

Now they sin more and more and have made them molten images of their silver, idols according to their own understanding, all of it the work of the craftsmen; they say of them, Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves. Remember the time frame and the other prophets that were prophesying during that time; the craftsman was making idols in the images of men. -
Therefore they shall be as the morning cloud, as the early dew that passeth away, as the chaff driven with the whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney.
Yet the Most High is the Lord thy God from the land of Egypt, and thou shalt know no god but him, for there is no saviour beside him.

He knew them in the wilderness, in the land of great drought. According to their pasture they were filled, and their heart was exalted; therefore they forgot him. That is what happens to us; when we get all the things we need, our food, water, and clothing, and a little excess, we forget the Lord.

Therefore he will be unto them as a lion, as a leopard by the way will he observe them; he will meet them as a bear bereaved of her whelps, rend the caul of their heart, and there devour them like a lion; the wild beast shall tear them.
O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself, but in the Most High is thine help.

He will be thy king; where is any other that may save thee in all thy cities, and thy judges of whom thou saidst, Give me a king and princes? The Lord is telling us there is none that saveth but him. -
He gave thee a king in his anger and took him away in his wrath.

The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up, his sin is hid. The sorrows of a travailing woman shall come upon him; he is an unwise son, for he should not stay long in the place of the breaking forth of children.
The Most High will ransom them from the power of the grave and redeem them from death; O death, he will be thy plagues; O grave, he will be thy destruction; repentance shall be hid from his eyes.

Though he be fruitful among his brethren, an east wind shall come, the wind of the Lord coming up from the wilderness, and his spring shall become dry and his fountain dried up; he shall spoil the treasure of all pleasant vessels.

Samaria shall become desolate, for she hath rebelled against her God; they shall fall by the sword, their infants dashed in pieces, and their women with child ripped up. This was a future prophecy at the time Hosea prophesied, about Assyria coming into the land. -

The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem, so that the habitations of the shepherds mourn and the top of Carmel withers. This chapter was read straight through without going precept upon precept.

For three transgressions of Damascus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron. He will send a fire into the house of Hazael that shall devour the palaces of Benhadad, break the bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitants of the plain of Aven and the sceptre from the house of Eden, and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir.

For three transgressions of Gaza and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they carried away the whole captivity to deliver them up to Edom. He will send a fire on the wall of Gaza that shall devour its palaces, cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the sceptre from Ashkelon, turn his hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish.

For three transgressions of Tyrus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and did not remember the brotherly covenant. He will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus that shall devour its palaces.

For three transgressions of Edom and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because Edom pursued his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and kept his wrath forever. He will send a fire upon Teman that shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.

For three transgressions of the children of Ammon and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge their border. He will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah that shall devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle and a tempest in the day of the whirlwind, and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)
